title: Promise Reduction Gap Hypothesis
statement: Let $q$ be a natural number with $\mathrm{Fin}(q)$ nonempty, let an encoded regular Unique Games family with alphabet size $q$ be given, and let an optimization encoding of that family and a binary promise problem be given. A gap hypothesis consists of real thresholds $s$ and $c$ with $s<c$, together with a promise-preserving Karp reduction from the given promise problem to the real-valued Unique Games gap problem determined by the encoding and these thresholds.
hypotheses_covered: an encoded regular Unique Games family with alphabet size $q$ is given
an optimization encoding of the family is given
a binary promise problem is given
soundness is strictly less than completeness
there is a Promise Karp reduction to the corresponding real-valued Unique Games gap problem
